scope: graph_indexer.py changed graph state, publication, producer lifecycle and direct snapshot reader

findings.title: Close the shared build connection on every exit
findings.problem: The publication cleanup changed from finally to an Exception handler plus success close. KeyboardInterrupt or another BaseException rolls back but skips close. New earlier acquisition also leaves ordinary exceptions in post-preparation reconciliation outside any closing arm. A retained exception traceback retains store and its actual APSW connection after build_index returns control and releases the build lock; __del__ cannot reclaim that connection until traceback lifetime ends.
findings.evidence: Public build_index on isolated temporary fixture with real APSW/SQLite and deterministic fake embeddings; injected KeyboardInterrupt at GraphPublication.apply. Retain caught exception, find store in traceback frame: connection still executes SELECT 1 => (1,), autocommit true, published census unchanged, build lock false. Separate OSError injection at _reap_stranded_vector_rows returns the same open connection result.
findings.expected: Connection already closed after failure/cancellation, including while the exception traceback remains retained.
findings.recommendation: Use unconditional finally covering each owned store's full lifetime, on both changed/full and idle paths; test retained traceback after cancellation and ordinary preparation/reconciliation errors.
findings.limits: P2 resource-lifetime failure in in-process callers retaining traceback. CLI process exit reclaims OS handles. Windows rename/delete interference is a possible platform consequence, not native-Windows-tested or claimed inevitable. Publication rollback itself worked.

findings.title: Pin the published graph helper to one read transaction
findings.problem: read_published_graph_snapshot says graph payload and source receipts come from one snapshot but never starts a read transaction. open_read_only likewise only opens and verifies schema. Its sequential SELECTs can straddle a concurrent atomic publication. server_impl._published_exact_definition_candidate removed its prior identity recheck relying on this promise; a new source receipt may therefore certify a node read from the old graph.
findings.evidence: Two native APSW connections in a temporary fixture: call original read_graph_payload_rows, commit node-label and source-hash updates on another connection, return to the helper's manifest read. Result has old label defined and new hash new_generation_hash. Control beginning a read transaction before payload read returns old label defined and old hash source-hash despite the same concurrent commit.
findings.expected: Payload and source receipt are both old, both new, or helper returns unavailable.
findings.recommendation: Begin one explicit read transaction before reading graph metadata, nodes, edges, and extraction manifest, and close it in finally. Add deterministic two-connection interleaving regression coverage.
findings.limits: Concurrency correctness issue on all supported OSes, not Windows-specific. Probe exercises helper with actual native storage, not full registered code_ask response.
